key_insight: A Gaussian surface bump significantly accelerates vortex-induced boundary-layer transition and the onset of three-dimensionality while preserving the spatio-temporal wave front characteristic of a nonmodal response.
engineering_relevance: Predicting transition over rough surfaces exposed to free-stream vortices requires three-dimensional modeling to capture the accelerated breakdown accurately.
method: Solve the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations using 2D and 3D direct numerical simulations.
Model a semi-infinite flat plate with a Gaussian bump and a convecting free-stream vortex of fixed strength and sign.
Analyze instantaneous flow features, vorticity dynamics, and nonlinear receptivity.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify four stages: roughness-generated vortical disturbances, spatio-temporal amplification, wave-front emergence with unsteady separation bubbles, and bubble merging into turbulent spots.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative transition shifts or parameter ranges, so applicability beyond the studied bump and vortex configuration remains uncertain.
paper_title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Vortex-Induced Instability Over a Semi-Infinite Flat Plate with Discrete Roughness
